text:
alex.k: Quick heads-up — I'm going to pilot a lightweight 'soft-isolate' evacuator in eu-west1 tonight (21:00 UTC). Not a full cordon+evacuate: it tries to steer new jobs away and gives running jobs a chance to finish/checkpoint. Reason: noisy ECC/Xid bursts are causing a lot of churn and unnecessary preempts.

maria_r: Nice. How is soft-isolate different from our existing soft-cordon flow?

alex.k: Good question — differences:
- taint vs hard-cordon: we apply a PreferNoSchedule taint so best-effort schedulers avoid the node rather than blocking everything.
- state machine: node moves soft->soft-isolate->hard-cordon only if signals persist for N minutes.
- probes: we debounce Xid/ECC spikes with a 3-sample sliding window, require >30% spike rate to escalate.

jonathan: Will this work for both K8s and Slurm clusters?

alex.k: Yes, it includes dual pathways. For K8s we taint/label; for Slurm we set NodeState=REQUEUE_PREP or a soft-drain flag that operators can opt into. Example commands we plan to use: 

```
# kubernetes path
kubectl label node gpu-12 redwood/soft-isolate=true
kubectl taint nodes gpu-12 redwood/soft-isolate=true:PreferNoSchedule
# fallback to full cordon after 15m if signals persist
kubectl cordon gpu-12
# slurm path (soft drain)
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-12 State=DRAIN Reason="soft-isolate (ECC spike)"
# allow running jobs to finish for up to 30m, then requeue if still flagged
```

lee: How do autoscalers react? We don't want ASG to terminate nodes still running long jobs.

alex.k: We'll tag soft-isolate nodes with lifecycle=evacuator and add a scale-in protection window (30m) so cloud-autoscaler ignores them for immediate termination. Also the probe service will annotate when it's safe to drop protection.

maria_r: Metrics/alerts? I want to know when it's flipping lots of nodes automatically.

ops-bot: [automated message] soft-isolate detector deployed to eu-west1 test pool. Alerts: slack @eng-infra if >5 nodes enter soft-isolate in 1h.

jonathan: What about KV cache and warm-up cost — if we constantly move pods we pay regen cost.

alex.k: Agree — that's why the default behavior is conservative: PreferNoSchedule -> wait 20-30m -> only escalate if repeated bursts. We'll also skip isolating nodes that have >70% cache hit ratio (from node telemetry) to avoid cold starts.

infra-oncall: If this lands we should have an easy manual override in console + a quick runbook in #incidents. Can we gate the rollout to non-critical pools first?

alex.k: Yes — rolling to test pool first (gpu-test*), then staging, then production pools by region. Runbook link will be posted before 21:00. Manual override CLI: `redwoodctl node unisolate gpu-12` and `kubectl untaint node gpu-12`

maria_r: Awesome. Can we also log an event in node metadata that records the signal history (count, timestamps) so SRE can triage replacements?

alex.k: Yep — plan is to push a small json blob to node annotations and to the fleet DB for easier query.

lee: One more ask — incremental backoff for repeated soft-isolates before we mark a node for replacement to reduce flapping.

alex.k: Backoff added: 1st isolate = 30m hold, 2nd = 2h, 3rd -> mark for replace and ping hardware team.

jonathan: sgtm. I'll review the hazard tests (simulated Xid bursts) tomorrow morning and validate autoscaler behaviour.

alex.k: Thanks all. I'll post the runbook and the canary pool list in 30m. Ping me if you want early access to the test pool. :thumbsup:
